mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of residence of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Samoa is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate shareholder or corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or licensed corporate services provider of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin followed by consular legalization through the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or nearest Samoan diplomatic post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account conduct, relationship tenure, and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating financial institution where the applicant maintains the referenced account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth and source of funds declaration with supporting documentation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin followed by consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional reference letters issued by a qualified lawyer, accountant, or corporate services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified professional in the country of origin of the applicant

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all directors, shareholders, registered agents, and UBOs against the UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury consolidated lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit domestic designations; mandatory PEP identification per Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 s.11(4); enhanced due diligence for all PEPs, their family members, and close associates; screening must be completed before incorporation and refreshed at least annually and upon any material change; all CDD records retained for a minimum of five years after termination of the business relationship; licensed registered agents must file STRs with the FIU and obtain approval for high-risk onboarding where the risk rating exceeds the medium threshold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - International Companies Registry; name clearance is lodged by a SIFA-licensed registered agent through the SIFA e-Registry pre-incorporation name reservation facility
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registered corporate name must be expressed in Latin script (English or Samoan) and must end with a permitted suffix such as Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, Pty Ltd, Ltd, or the Samoan equivalent; the International Companies Act 1987 does not recognize Chinese characters for statutory registration purposes; a Chinese trade name may be adopted for commercial convenience and reflected in internal records and the company seal, but the statutory name remains the Latin-script name; any transliteration must not create phonetic or visual confusion with an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the licensed registered agent must submit a written representation to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, including supporting letters of consent from holders of any identical or confusingly similar names, and, for sensitive tokens, prior written approval from the relevant ministry or sector regulator; if the Registrar upholds the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Minister for Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 calendar days of the final decision; a further application for judicial review lies to the Supreme Court of Samoa within 42 days of the Ministerial determination; name reservations may be renewed once for a further 30-day period by re-filing the reservation application and paying the applicable fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a substitute: International Companies Act 1987 requires a physical registered office address located in Samoa, maintained under the custody of a SIFA-licensed registered agent who must be physically present in Samoa; the registered office must house the statutory registers, minute books, and beneficial ownership records; a virtual office or remote mail-forwarding address may be used for ancillary correspondence only and cannot satisfy the statutory registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium - SIFA conducts risk-based AML/CFT on-site inspections of licensed registered agents; the supervisory program contemplates physical inspection of the registered agent's premises, client files, and UBO registers on a cycle of approximately once every two to three years per agent; the risk of inspection is materially elevated where the portfolio services predominantly non-resident clients, involves higher-risk jurisdictions, or where adverse intelligence or third-party reporting flags the agent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987, as amended, ss 6 (incorporation), 11 (registered office), and 78 (registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registration and Licensing Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Application for Incorporation of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; International Companies may issue shares with or without par value and capital may be wholly unpaid until the first board determines otherwise
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Memorandum and Articles of Association, as filed with SIFA, are adopted in final form; (2) the subscribers subscribe for one International Company share of no par value at the issue price fixed by the director, and the share register is opened; (3) the registered office be fixed at 2nd Floor, SIFA Centre, Apia, Samoa, and the registered agent be appointed; (4) John Doe is appointed as sole director and Jane Doe as secretary, each to hold office until the next annual meeting; (5) the filing of such incorporation application and the payment of government fees are ratified; (6) the director and secretary are authorised to open bank accounts and affix the common seal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of SIFA-licensed registered agent and corporate name pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Registration Desk; through a SIFA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the intended corporate name and a brief statement of proposed activities to the registered agent for pre-clearance against the SIFA name-protection index. The agent prepares the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association and obtains a signed engagement letter before any formal filing. If the name is available, the agent reserves it pending receipt of the executed incorporation package.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter with licensed registered agent
Corporate name availability request form
Passport copy of each proposed shareholder
Proof of residential address of each proposed shareholder
Bank and professional references
Brief statement of proposed business activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected to, submit up to three alternative names with justifications; any similar name may be cleared on receipt of a consent letter from the existing holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of constitutional incorporation instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and notary public or equivalent testamentary officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the Memorandum and Articles of Association, execute the application for incorporation, and obtain consents from the proposed director, secretary, and registered agent. All signatures must be witnessed and, if required by the board or governing rules, notarised or apostilled. The registered agent conducts identity and background verification consistent with Samoa AML/CFT requirements.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association in final form
Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Consent of registered agent
Consent of director and secretary
Verification certificates under the SIFA licensed agent AML/CFT policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the executing officer identifies stamping or notarisation defects, the affected signature pages are re-executed by the same or substitute signatory and a corrected duplicate package is prepared at no additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to SIFA and payment of statutory fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Registration and Licensing Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits the completed incorporation package, together with the SIFA cover sheet and proof of due diligence, and pays the official state filing fee by bank wire or direct deposit. SIFA issues a fee receipt and assigns a pending file number. The applicant must respond promptly to any SIFA query within the statutory notice window.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consents of first director, secretary, and registered agent
AML/CFT due diligence file kept by the registered agent
Payment remittance slip for USD 200 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a query requiring clarification, submit a supplementary statutory declaration within 14 calendar days; SIFA may also require a corrected schedule of shareholders or restated articles, after which processing is resumed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and opening of statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Registration and Licensing Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, SIFA issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a certified copy of the articles. The registered agent then prepares the share register, registers of directors, secretary and charges, and the common seal, and files the registered office details in the SIFA database.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by SIFA
Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association
Register of Members
Register of Directors and Secretary
Register of Charges
Registered office consent from the premises owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains typographical errors or the statutory registers are rejected, submit a written request with the original certificate and pay only the administrative replacement fee for a corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, adoption of corporate governance minutes, and banking onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors, secretary, and licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Call the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent adopting the formal board resolution, sealing the common seal, approving opening of a bank account, and setting the annual return date. The registered agent prepares the minutes, maintains the statutory registers, and files any annual return calendar in the SIFA portal.
required_dossiers: Signed minutes of the first board meeting or written consent resolution
Form appointing the registered agent and registered office
Share certificates executed under seal
Bank account opening package containing Certificate of Incorporation, articles, and due diligence forms
Written consent actions of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If minutes are challenged by a banker or counterparty, re-execute the resolution by unanimous written consent with the same substance and affix the common seal; any irregularly issued share certificate must be cancelled and reissued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) in coordination with Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for offshore commercial secretarial services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Company Management or Registered Agent Operating Licence under the International Companies Act 1987 and allied SIFA licensing regime

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (low-impact office activity); no full EIA report required for a registered-agent and secretarial office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Samoa Wastewater discharge limits into municipal sewer for sanitary-only effluent; no industrial point-source discharge; premises must comply with the Waste Management Act for segregated paper and electronic waste; no VOC or combustion emission sources are installed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for the registered office from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; structural load inspection certificate confirming office floor loading for safes and records; workplace clearance issued by MCIL labour inspectorate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Apia, Samoa - integrated tax and customs administration; official portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws (eServices for TIN registration, VAT registration, monthly returns and customs declarations). The Registrar of International Companies within the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) administers company incorporation and annual returns; SRA issues all tax registrations and certificates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - The licensed Samoa registered agent (ICSP) files the SRA TIN application (company TIN registration form) on behalf of the International Company (IC), attaching the certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, director and shareholder register, notarized passport copies of all beneficial owners, and certified proof of the registered office in Samoa. Step 2 - SRA performs KYC/AML screening and issues the TIN, which is also used for CRS/FATCA reporting. Step 3 - The IC obtains a Certificate of Tax Exemption from SRA/Registrar confirming exemption under the International Companies Act 2018 and the Income Tax Act 2015; this certificate is required by international banks and foreign counterparties. Step 4 - The agent pays the annual government fee (USD 100) and files the exempt-company annual return with the Registrar; the IC files no income tax return because it derives no Samoan-source taxable income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: A Samoa International Company is a non-resident exempt entity for all Samoan direct and indirect taxes. Foreign-source income, including registered-agent, company-secretarial and corporate administration fees from offshore clients, is wholly exempt from income tax; no capital gains tax, no dividend, interest or royalty withholding taxes on offshore payments, no estate or gift duty, and no business license tax on offshore activities. The exemption is forfeited if the IC carries on a commercial business in Samoa; the International Companies Act 2018 prohibits domestic trading and permits only concessionary acts such as contracting with the Government of Samoa, holding director meetings, maintaining a bank account, and transacting securities dealings with other exempt offshore entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Samoa; the IC's exempt status is fixed by statute. Available statutory elections: (1) voluntary VAT registration under the VAT Act 2008 s.10 for supplies below the compulsory threshold, practically applicable only if the IC were to engage in permitted domestic supplies; (2) an election by the IC to convert to a Domestic Company under the International Companies Act 2018, thereby entering entity-level taxation at the resident corporate income tax rate (27% headline, 2015 Act) on worldwide income; (3) CRS/FATCA classification elections to be treated as a non-financial entity, an investment entity or a reporting financial institution; (4) transitional elections for foreign companies to redomicile into Samoa as International Companies. Samoa has not enacted domestic hybrid-mismatch rules; BEPS-aligned outcomes depend on treaty application and the Multilateral Convention.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - VAT Act 2008 and Taxes Administration Act 2012, administered by the Samoa Revenue Authority; the scheme replaced the former Goods and Services Tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WS$ 100,000 (SAT 100,000) of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period for a business carried on in Samoa (VAT Act 2008 s.9); voluntary registration is available below the threshold but is factually inapplicable to an exempt International Company deriving only offshore income.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or e-invoicing API mandate exists in Samoa. SRA requires a VAT-compliant tax invoice containing the mandatory particulars under VAT Act 2008 s.18 (supplier name and TIN, recipient name and TIN, invoice date, serial number, description, quantity, taxable value, VAT amount or zero-rated indicator). Electronic invoices are accepted without fiscal-printer certification or government API integration. Customs declarations are lodged through the ASYCUDA World electronic single window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) goods physically exported from Samoa, evidenced by removal within the statutory period; (2) exported services, including offshore secretarial, corporate administration and registered-agent services, supplied to a non-resident person who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and not directly connected with land in Samoa or with movable property in Samoa; (3) international transport, insurance, and supplies to diplomatic missions. Registered-agent services supplied by an International Company to another International Company qualify as exported services where the recipient is non-resident and there is no direct land nexus; the separately designated statutory 'maintenance of registered office' element carries a legal-seat nexus with Samoa and requires a documented non-resident-client declaration and legal analysis. Input VAT attributable to the exempt offshore business is not creditable unless the corresponding supply is properly zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged electronically via ASYCUDA World (SRA Customs)
Bill of Lading, Master or House Air Waybill, or postal dispatch evidence
Commercial invoice and VAT zero-rated tax invoice compliant with VAT Act 2008 s.18
Executed service agreement or contract evidencing the offshore service
Non-Resident Client Declaration or certificate of foreign residence
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank advice proving receipt of export proceeds through a licensed Samoa commercial bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA may reassess and claw back zero-rated input VAT credits and refunds within 4 years of the relevant tax period, with no limitation period for fraud or willful evasion (Taxes Administration Act 2012). Penalties: shortfall penalties of 25% for careless conduct, up to 50% for intentional understatement, and up to 100% or more for deliberate evasion; default interest applies at 2% per month, compounding; criminal prosecution of directors and registered agents carries fines of up to WS$ 200,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years for fraudulent zero-rating claims. The Registrar may additionally suspend or revoke the ICSP license upon false certification, and the client International Company may lose its Certificate of Tax Exemption retrospectively.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and responsible for administering the Exchange Control Act 1977 and all Exchange Control Notices issued thereunder.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa maintains a managed-float currency regime for the Samoan Tala (WST). Current-account payments such as trade, services, wages and remittances are generally permitted through authorised dealers with underlying documentation. Capital-account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment, foreign-currency borrowing, intercompany shareholder loans, cross-border guarantees and portfolio flows, are subject to prior Central Bank of Samoa approval or a post-transaction notification requirement. For a non-resident-owned Samoan International Company, the entity is exempt from Samoa income tax on foreign-sourced income, but an outward remittance of WST profits or dividends will be processed only after the authorised dealer verifies a board resolution, audited or management financial statements, an international company good-standing certificate, a beneficial-ownership declaration and confirmation that the ultimate recipient is not a sanctioned person. The practical hurdle is therefore not tax, but the enhanced due diligence required to establish source of funds and the absence of any Samoa exchange-control objection.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1977 and Central Bank of Samoa notices, exporters must arrange for export proceeds to be repatriated to Samoa through an authorised dealer within 90 days from the date of export. The default statutory surrender obligation is 100% conversion of the foreign-currency export invoice value into WST, unless the exporter obtains a Central Bank of Samoa foreign-currency retention licence or operates as a tax-exempt International Company with an approved foreign-currency account. For ISIC 8299 registered-agent and offshore secretarial services, there is no physical export of goods; cross-border fee receivables are treated as current-account receipts, must be received by wire through a licensed authorised dealer, and the entity may retain or convert the foreign currency only with bank-recorded exchange-control reporting and source-of-funds documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited - Samoa Branch (BSP Samoa)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, supplementary corridor only. Legal constraints: Samoa does not license independent non-resident fintech electronic-money institutions. Any entity accepting deposits or issuing e-money in Samoa must be licensed by the Central Bank of Samoa under the Financial Institutions Act 2007 and the applicable AML/CFT regulations. Non-resident digital EMIs, such as Mercury, Revolut Business or Airwallex, may onboard a Samoa International Company as a remote corporate client, but they cannot provide a Samoa-local clearing account or hold client funds as a Samoa-regulated money-transfer business. Relying on such an EMI as the primary treasury account creates legal, sanctions and asset-isolation risks and will be treated as an adverse structural red flag by local regulated banks. Accordingly, foreign EMIs may be used only for low-volume cross-border professional-fee receipts, with full disclosure to the Samoa bank and registered agent, and must never be used for client money or regulatory capital.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, physical presence is mandatory for a newly formed Samoa International Company. At least one substantive director, the beneficial owner and any authorised signatory must attend an in-person identity verification interview at the Apia head office or an approved overseas branch of the banking group. Remote video-KYC onboarding is possible only where the applicant is an existing banking-group client and the Samoa-licensed registered agent provides a signed attestation under the AML/CTF Act. Each director must provide a passport, proof of residential address, professional reference, corporate registry extract and source-of-wealth evidence. Bank compliance will also require the original certificate of incorporation, board resolutions, share register and beneficial-ownership declarations before any account is opened.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore secretarial entity with no physical office, no staff, no audited financial statements and a shared registered-agent address, giving the appearance of insufficient economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International Company certificate of incorporation; International Companies Registry annual return and good-standing certificate; registered-agent licence; constitution and board resolutions; adverse-beneficial-ownership register with full KYC data of shareholders; an independent legal opinion confirming tax-exempt offshore status and the absence of Samoan-source income; three years of management accounts or bank statements; source-of-wealth declaration; and a signed registered-agent AML attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership through discretionary trusts, protected-cell structures, nominee directors or nominee shareholders that obscures the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed or trust certificate identifying settlor and protector; UBO ownership chart showing all 25% thresholds; written declaration from each nominee shareholder/director confirming capacity and control; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; certified passport copies of all natural persons in the ownership chain; independent legal opinion that no bearer shares or unregistered share instruments exist; and a bank reference from the trustee's or nominee's own financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border fund flows from high-risk jurisdictions and repeated third-party disbursements that are inconsistent with statutory company secretarial fee revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 8299 fee-earning contracts for company formation, registered-office and secretarial services; itemised invoice ledger with pricing and counterparty details; payment-flow diagrams and SWIFT purpose codes; corporate registry extracts for counterparties; AML clearance from originating financial institutions; internal client acceptance file; registered-agent regulatory approval; and an AML compliance officer attestation confirming enhanced monitoring and transaction-activity consistency.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas remitting bank to the Samoa authorised dealer bank. The beneficiary field must state the exact legal name of the Samoa International Company and include the International Companies Registry number in the beneficiary-reference line. The remitter must use the home-jurisdiction outward remittance purpose code for equity investment or capital transfer; for example, 'equity capital', 'capital transfer' or 'loan disbursement' as recognised by the sending bank's classification system. The Samoa receiving bank will pre-clear the wire against a board resolution authorising the capital call, the share subscription agreement, the share register and source-of-funds documentation. Wires incorrectly described as 'consultancy' or 'trade payments' will be rejected or frozen. Any shareholder loan exceeding USD 10,000 must be supported by a written facility agreement and reported to the Central Bank of Samoa exchange-control section through the authorised dealer within the prescribed notification window, or the company may face Exchange Control Act penalties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements from a Samoa International Company are cleared through the authorised dealer's correspondent banking network. For professional-fee invoices and general operational disbursements, the preferred rail is a SWIFT MT103 from the IC's USD or WST account, with the beneficiary account information, the relevant reference for the invoice and the exchange-control declaration if the amount exceeds the WST-equivalent threshold of USD 50,000. For goods-based trade settlements, the acceptable rail is an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 or MT720, with the Samoa authorised dealer acting as issuing or advising bank. USD settlements are cleared via CHIPS or Fedwire through New York correspondents; AUD and NZD settlements use local clearing systems; WST settlements are domestic and require a licensed authorised dealer transaction. The bank will require invoices, director resolutions and any applicable exchange-control declaration before execution. Payments to sanctioned entities or people are absolutely prohibited, and recurring disbursements to connected treasury companies must be supported by group transfer-pricing documentation to prevent AML structuring classification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts up to 12 months, transacted through a licensed authorised dealer in Samoa, supported by an underlying commercial receivable or payable in WST versus USD/AUD/EUR.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps and FX swaps involving a two-currency principal exchange, used only to hedge foreign-currency shareholder loans or long-term intercompany balances, subject to Central Bank of Samoa prior notification or approval.
Purchased FX options, not short options, limited to hedging fee receipts, dividend remittances or committed disbursements, with CBS-compliant confirmation and no speculative premium harvesting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST only where the counterparty is a licensed international bank and the Central Bank of Samoa has issued a specific hedge-authorisation letter; speculative uncovered NDFs and cryptocurrency derivatives are not permissible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; the IFA accepts filings up to the last business day of the anniversary month in practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 100 per month or part thereof; up to WST 1,000; continued default triggers administrative strike-off and potential dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually by 30 June for the ensuing year, or pro-rated for new international companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of unpaid fee if not paid by due date; further penalties accrue monthly; persistent non-payment may result in license revocation and strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (licensed offshore service provider) and IFA upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deliverable to the registered agent within 30 days of each anniversary of incorporation for confirmation of registered details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm exposes the company to non-compliance findings by the registered agent and regulatory reporting to the IFA; continuous failure may lead to strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tax Exemption Status Declaration / Nil Tax Return (where required by IFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Inland Revenue Division / Ministry of Revenue via IFA process
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No general annual tax return for international companies; nil declaration required only upon specific IFA or Inland Revenue request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond to a statutory request may result in penalties under the International Companies Act; possible loss of tax-exempt status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 2012; an audit may be required if the company is a large international company notified by the IFA, if the company's shareholders holding at least 5% of shares request an audit, or if the company is licensed to conduct banking, insurance, or trust business
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory accounting standard is prescribed for a standard international company; where financial records are prepared for audit or external use, the company may adopt IFRS or a jurisdictionally recognized local GAAP; the International Companies Act requires records sufficient to show transactions and financial position

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain a current beneficial ownership register under the International Companies Act and the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) requirements; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be notified to the registered agent immediately and in all cases before the filing of the annual confirmation; the annual confirmation protocol requires the directors to confirm the accuracy of the register of members, directors, and beneficial owners at each anniversary; there is no separate public UBO filing with the IFA, but the registered agent must make the register available to the IFA upon request

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 8,500 per annum for a small international company when an audit is voluntarily or contractually required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) are wholly exempt from Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, and all other direct taxes. No tax returns are required to be filed with the Ministry for Revenue. The only fiscal charge is the annual Government fee paid to the Registrar of International Companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No income tax return is required for an International Company. The sole annual compliance obligation is the Annual Return on Form IC-AR filed with the Samoa International Companies Office (Registrar) via the online portal of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) at www.mcil.gov.ws or through a licensed registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return must be filed within 28 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation. For a company incorporated on 1 January, the return is due by 28 January each year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company number, registered name, date of incorporation, and jurisdiction of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name and number exactly as recorded on the Certificate of Incorporation. Non-resident beneficial owners need not be disclosed on the public return. A separate confidential beneficial ownership register is maintained with the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address of the registered office in Samoa, which must be maintained by a licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the full street address and the name of the registered agent. P.O. boxes are not acceptable as a registered office. The address must be a physical location in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of all directors, the secretary, and the registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors may be listed. The company must have at least one director and one secretary; the secretary may be the registered agent. A director need not be resident in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized capital, issued capital, and class of shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the par value and paid-up amount. For no-par-value shares, mark 'NPV'. Nominee shareholders are permitted; the underlying beneficial owner may be recorded in the confidential register only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by a director or the registered agent that the company has not carried on business in Samoa, has not derived income from Samoa, and has no real property in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the declaration. If income was derived from Samoan domestic sources, the company would cease to be eligible for IC status and become subject to ordinary Samoan income tax at 27%. This declaration is critical for maintaining tax-exempt status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Annual Return on time incurs a late filing fee of WST 200 for the first month and WST 50 per month thereafter, up to a maximum of WST 500. Further default may lead to automatic striking-off of the company from the Register, forfeiture of assets to the Crown, and personal liability for directors for debts contracted during the period of default. Criminal fines of up to WST 1,000 may apply for false declarations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is required because Samoa does not impose any withholding tax on dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders. Similarly, no Samoa withholding tax is levied on repatriation of profits, return of capital, or liquidation distributions. If a shareholder resides in a jurisdiction having a double tax agreement with Samoa (only a limited network, e.g. Samoa has no broad DTA network; it has tax information exchange agreements), the shareholder may rely on the exemption unilaterally. No Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from Samoa is necessary for the IC itself because the IC is non-resident for Samoan tax purposes and is not taxed. A foreign shareholder may obtain a Samoan TRC only in respect of residual items, but for IC distributions the 0% statutory rate cannot be improved by treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Samoa does not impose withholding tax on interest or royalties paid by an International Company to non-residents. This applies to all cross-border interest on shareholder loans, intercompany debt, and royalties for intellectual property licensed into or out of the IC. No Samoan tax deduction is available to the IC for such payments because the IC is outside the Samoan income tax net, but no WHT is chargeable at source. Treaty/non-treaty rates are effectively nil.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: N/A – International Companies are outside the scope of Samoa's Income Tax Act 2012 (which contains no specific transfer pricing rules but applies only to domestic taxable entities). However, the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020 imposes substance filing thresholds. For an IC with gross annual income from relevant geographies exceeding SAT 1,000,000 (approx. USD 370,000), the company must file an Economic Substance Return and maintain a Local File-style record of core income-generating activities, including evidence of management, employees, premises, and expenditure in Samoa. Master File documentation is not statutorily mandated, but prudent practice for an IC in the registered agent/secretarial sector with cross-border related-party transactions is to prepare a thin-capitalization memorandum and a TP policy summary.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Yes. The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020 (as amended) applies. A Samoa International Company must demonstrate economic substance in Samoa proportionate to its activity. For the registered agent and corporate secretarial business, the relevant activity is 'Headquarters and similar services' and 'Services to related parties'. The company must show: (a) a physical office in Samoa; (b) at least one employee in Samoa (can be a licensed registered agent's employee if acting as the company's secretary); (c) annual operating expenditure in Samoa (e.g. WST 20,000–50,000 depending on turnover); (d) board meetings held in Samoa at least once per year; and (e) records and corporate minutes stored in Samoa. Failure to satisfy ESR results in penalties and possible automatic strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An International Company carrying on any commercial, industrial, financial, professional, or other business with any person resident in Samoa, or deriving income from any Samoan source, while continuing to declare itself tax-exempt as an IC. This includes providing registered agent services to Samoan domestic residents or managing domestic trusts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of exempt status; retrospective taxation of all profits derived from Samoa at the 27% corporate income tax rate; interest on unpaid tax at 12% per annum; penalty of 200% of the tax evaded under the Income Tax Act 2012; criminal fine up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 7 years for willful evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they signed the false declaration or knowingly permitted the company to engage in Samoan domestic business. Travel bans may be issued by the Samoan Ministry for Revenue, and directors may be subject to extradition under mutual assistance treaties. Imprisonment of up to 7 years applies to fraudulent tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a passive shell with no economic substance, no physical office in Samoa, no employees in Samoa, no active SPV activities, and with all corporate decisions made outside Samoa, while claiming IC status solely to avoid tax under the OECD/G20 Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020, the Registrar may impose a penalty of WST 500 per day up to WST 100,000 for failure to meet economic substance. The company may be struck off the Register; the Court may order the winding-up of the company and forfeiture of assets located in Samoa. The tax-exempt status is revoked retroactively, and a 100% surcharge on any unpaid tax may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell IC may be held personally liable for the company's tax liabilities up to the amount of distributions or payments received from the company. The Samoan Court can issue a director disqualification order, a travel ban, and a restitution order requiring disgorgement of profits. In egregious cases, directors can be prosecuted for fraudulent trading (penalty up to 5 years' imprisonment).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC fails to maintain a beneficial ownership register, fails to file an Economic Substance Return, or deliberately disguises the ultimate beneficial owner to facilitate money laundering through nominee director arrangements, or the registered agent fails to conduct enhanced due diligence on non-resident clients under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2023.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties range from WST 50,000 to WST 250,000 for each breach. The registered agent's license may be suspended or revoked. The IC may be struck off. Individuals knowingly involved can face a fine of WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Any assets derived from criminal conduct are subject to civil forfeiture under the Proceeds of Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent face personal criminal liability for failing to comply with AML requirements. Civil penalties include restitution of all illicit gains, a travel ban, and a 10-year prohibition from acting as a director of any Samoa registered company. Imprisonment up to 5 years applies for money laundering offenses. The statutory presumption of directorial knowledge in AML cases shifts the burden of proof to the director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Return and ESR Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to submit the Annual Return (Form IC-AR) within 28 days of the anniversary of incorporation and failing to file the annual Economic Substance Return (ESR-01) with MCIL within the same deadline, when the company exceeds the ESR threshold or falls within a relevant activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing fee of WST 200 plus WST 50 per month for the Annual Return. Independently, the ESR regime imposes a fixed penalty of WST 500 for initial non-filing, WST 1,000 for continuing non-filing, and WST 10,000 for knowingly filing a false ESR return, plus a daily default penalty of WST 100 per day. The Registrar may strike off the company after 6 months of default, resulting in the transfer of all the company's property to the Samoan Crown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for all debts and liabilities of the company incurred after the date of default if the company continues to trade while struck off. Further, directors who sign a false ESR declaration face criminal penalties of a fine up to WST 50,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years. A civil restitution order may compel a director to reimburse the company for any tax advantage gained.
